record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: A continuous operator V on S^{m-1} is called bistochastic when V(x) is majorized by x for every x in the simplex. For quadratic stochastic operators satisfying this bistochastic majorization condition, describe the behavior of trajectories: convergence or non-convergence, possible limit sets, recurrent behavior, and the way the majorization constraint shapes the orbit structure.

evidence.quote: Definition 4. An arbitrary continuous operator V : S m−1 → S m−1 satisfying the condition V (x) ≺ x, x ∈ S m−1 is called a bistochastic operator.
Problem 13. Investigate the behavior of trajectories of the bistochastic quadratic operators.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m : x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. For $x,y\in S^{m-1}$, write $y\prec x$ (y is majorized by x) if, after rearranging the coordinates in non-increasing order $x_{[1]}\ge\cdots\ge x_{[m]}$ and $y_{[1]}\ge\cdots\ge y_{[m]}$, one has $\sum_{i=1}^k y_{[i]}\le\sum_{i=1}^k x_{[i]}$ for all $k=1,\dots,m-1$ (with equality at $k=m$). A continuous map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ is called bistochastic if $V(x)\prec x$ for every $x\in S^{m-1}$. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ of the form $(V(x))_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\,x_i x_j$, where the coefficients satisfy $p_{ij,k}=p_{ji,k}\ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$.

For every bistochastic quadratic stochastic operator $V$ on $S^{m-1}$, describe the asymptotic behavior of the trajectories $\{V^n(x)\}_{n\ge 0}$ for arbitrary initial point $x\in S^{m-1}$: determine whether the orbit converges, characterize the possible $\omega$-limit sets and recurrent behavior, identify and classify the fixed points, and explain how the majorization constraint $V(x)\prec x$ structures the orbit dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of describing trajectory behavior of bistochastic QSOs remains open. Partial progress exists: subclasses such as b-bistochastic QSOs (defined via a related b-order) have been studied, with classifications of fixed points (attracting/repelling/saddle/non-hyperbolic) and convergence results for specific low-dimensional cases. Surveys on QSO dynamics continue to list the general dynamical behavior of bistochastic QSOs as a difficult, largely unresolved problem.

status_evidence.title: On b-bistochastic quadratic stochastic operators
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces b-bistochastic QSOs; classifies fixed points and studies dynamics for special classes.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on bistochastic-type QSO dynamics exist for the b-order subclass.

status_evidence.title: On dynamics of quadratic stochastic operators: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey indicating limit behavior and ergodic properties of QSO trajectories remain generally difficult and open.
status_evidence.claim: General trajectory behavior of bistochastic QSOs is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Doubly stochastic operators on a finite-dimensional simplex
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bistochastic (doubly stochastic) operators on the simplex with majorization condition.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses bistochastic operators but does not fully resolve the QSO trajectory problem.
